messages:
sara: FYI — AcmeAI reported a steady stream of 502/504s hitting their hosted API since ~09:12 UTC. Customer is seeing failures on long-lived streaming calls.
eli: Got it. Are there request IDs or sample traces?
sara: Customer shared a sample trace id: trace:acme-0a1b2c3d and a curl repro. They said it started after a model swap.
maya: Pasting their curl (sanitized):
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/streaming/generate \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-large-quant","input":"stream test","stream":true}'
```
eli: When we repro locally we see the connection open then Envoy upstream rst after ~30s for some streams.
jordan: Monitoring shows an ingress gateway spike at 09:11–09:25 UTC, 502 rate went from 0.2% -> 8% for the tenant slice.
monitoring-bot: [alert] edge-gateway_502_rate > 5% for tenant=acmeai in cluster=us-west-2 (09:13 UTC)
sara: Customer is asking if this is a billing/auth issue — they see 502s intermittently followed by successful retries.
eli: Check auth backend logs? If auth service stalls, upstream returns 502 via midfront. I’m pulling auth latency histogram.
maya: I looked at auth logs for the tenant around 09:12: there are spikes of 500ms verification calls and a few 502 responses from billing-proxy (internal). Sample request_id: req-0f9c.
jordan: Also seeing a short-lived increase in concurrent keepalive count exhaustion on the frontdoor pool. Connection_pool_in_use peaked.
sre-oncall: Oncall here — can you paste a stacktrace or full upstream response body from one failed request?
sara: From customer curl verbose: 
```
> POST /v1/streaming/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.example
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< content-type: application/json
< x-request-id: req-0f9c
< x-edge-proxy: envoy
{
  "error": "upstream reset: connection reset by peer"
}
```
eli: That matches Envoy upstream RST. Need to correlate with midproxy/backends.
maya: I see a pattern: large streaming sessions + model swap = sudden KV cache invalidation on serving runtime which causes short auth/billing backend bursts. Could cause connection resets while we rebind upstreams.
jordan: I’m pulling the frontdoor upstream logs for those req ids now. If it's a pool exhaustion we should see 5xxs with upstream_reset type WINDOW or CONNECTION_FAILURE.
sre-oncall: If we can repro, try toggling model variant to fallback to non-quantized instance to see if failure disappears (we suspect runtime hot-swap interaction).
sara: Customer willing to try fallback, asking for a safe mitigation they can apply without breaking traffic.
eli: Quick mitigation: enable client retry with exponential backoff (they already have retries but lower backoff). Also we can apply a temporary routing rule to pin them to stable model instance pool.
maya: From logs: upstream reset_type=CONNECTION_FAILURE, reason=local reset, code=0. Suggests upstream closed before Envoy finished streaming.
jordan: I forwarded matching trace to eng-runtime (trace:acme-0a1b2c3d). Also attached dashboard link: https://monitoring.redwood.example/d/edge/tenant-acmeai?from=1712349000&to=1712350500
sre-oncall: I'm going to increase frontdoor keepalive pool size by +20% in us-west-2 as a temporary mitigation. Will monitor for 10 mins.
monitoring-bot: [runbook] increased keepalive pool for cluster=us-west-2 by 20% (actioned by sre-oncall)
sara: Customer applied client-side retry with 500ms jitter. They report error rate dropped but still see rare 502s on long streams.
eli: Next steps: eng-runtime to look at model swap code path and KV cache invalidation interaction with upstream placeholders. Tagging @eng-runtime.
maya: I’ve captured heap and thread dumps for serving instances that handled the swaps at 09:10–09:14. Uploading to secure bucket and sharing link in eng-runtime channel.
jordan: Added temporary canary rule to route AcmeAI traffic to pinned instance group (no model swap) — should eliminate swap-related resets.
sre-oncall: Pool increase holding. 502 rate for tenant down to ~1.1% over last 3m. Keeping watch.
sara: Customer is satisfied for now but requested ETA for permanent fix and notes this impacted their SLAs.
eli: Eng-runtime: prioritize a fix for graceful upstream handoff during model hot-swap, add regression test for long-lived streaming sessions.
maya: Will create an RFC and a small patch. Also add a monitoring alert for model-swap-induced 502 spikes.
sre-oncall: Marking incident as mitigated. Please file a customer postmortem and next-action items.
sara: Thanks — I'll open the support ticket update and schedule a follow-up with AcmeAI. :thumbsup:
summary: Support thread: AcmeAI reported streaming 502/504 spike after model swap. Team observed Envoy upstream resets and frontdoor keepalive exhaustion. Temporary mitigations: increase pool size, route tenant to pinned instance group, client retry. Next: eng-runtime to fix model hot-swap upstream handoff and add tests/alerts.
